A simulation spec from any R function

Source: R/sim-function.R
sim_function.Rd

Wraps a function fn(..., seed) that runs one replicate and returns a named list (or one-row data frame) of outcomes, or a single number (stored as value). Arguments given here are passed to fn; set any of them to tune() and give its range in params.

Usage

sim_function(fn, ..., params = list(), check = NULL, metrics = NULL)

Arguments

fn

A function whose arguments include the ones given in ... and seed.

...

Arguments for fn; use tune() to mark one for tuning.

params

Named list of dials parameter objects giving default ranges for tuned arguments (see sim_param()).

check

Optional function of the same arguments returning NULL when a design is feasible or a reason string when it is not.

metrics

Optional default sim_metric_set().

Value

A sim_function spec.

Examples

toy <- sim_function(
  function(x, noise, seed) {
    set.seed(seed)
    list(y = -(x - 3)^2 + rnorm(1, sd = noise))
  },
  x = tune(), noise = 0.5,
  params = list(x = sim_param(c(0, 6)))
)
res <- tune_grid(toy, sim_replicates(5), grid = 7,
                 metrics = sim_metric_set(sim_metric("y", "maximize")))
show_best(res, n = 2)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>       x .metric   mean     n std_err .config  
#>   <int> <chr>    <dbl> <int>   <dbl> <chr>    
#> 1     3 y       -0.311     5   0.109 Config004
#> 2     2 y       -1.31      5   0.109 Config003
